unit: one complete dynamic job trace simulated on the fixed homogeneous GPU-cluster specification, throughput table, configuration, and seed

metrics.name: makespan_seconds
metrics.means: The simulated elapsed time in seconds from the trace's start until all jobs selected for completion have finished.
metrics.source: upstream/scheduler/scripts/drivers/simulate_scheduler_with_trace.py (the value returned by sched.simulate and stored as pickle key makespan)

metrics.name: average_jct_seconds
metrics.means: The arithmetic mean, in seconds, of the simulated completion durations of all jobs selected for completion in this trace.
metrics.source: upstream/scheduler/scheduler.py::Scheduler.get_average_jct; emitted by upstream/scheduler/scripts/drivers/simulate_scheduler_with_trace.py as pickle key avg_jct

metrics.name: worst_finish_time_fairness_rho
metrics.means: The maximum across jobs in the trace of finish-time-fairness rho, where each job's rho is its completion duration divided by its exclusive running time times max(1, number_of_jobs_in_trace / number_of_gpus).
metrics.source: upstream/scheduler/scheduler.py::Scheduler.get_finish_time_fairness computes finish_time_fairness_list; upstream/scheduler/reproduce/aggregate_result.py reports worst_ftf as max(finish_time_fairness_list)

metrics.name: unfair_job_fraction_percent
metrics.means: The percentage of jobs in the trace whose finish-time-fairness rho is greater than the artifact's published fairness threshold 1.05, rounded to two decimal places exactly as in the artifact.
metrics.source: upstream/scheduler/reproduce/aggregate_result.py (FTF_FAIRNESS_THRESHOLD = 1.05 and unfair_fractions); its input finish_time_fairness_list is produced by upstream/scheduler/scheduler.py::Scheduler.get_finish_time_fairness

continuous_score.aggregation: raw binary64 arithmetic mean across the two selected workloads; no evaluator rounding

domain.worst_finish_time_fairness_rho: [0.5,+infinity) because original N/G is 8/4 and completion cannot beat exclusive runtime

continuous_score.upper_bound: 100 only at the natural joint optimum M=0, J=0, rho=0.5, U=0; no finite artificial clipping

beats_reference: Compute the four strict lower-is-better comparisons independently on each of the two graded traces. beats_reference is 1 if and only if all eight workload/metric comparisons pass. Otherwise it is 0. The continuous score remains independent and does not affect this binary verdict.

solver_feedback.name: makespan_seconds
solver_feedback.means: The candidate's own makespan in seconds for each workload trace.
solver_feedback.reveals_reference: no — it is an absolute measurement of only the candidate run and contains no reference-relative term.

solver_feedback.name: average_jct_seconds
solver_feedback.means: The candidate's own average job completion time in seconds for each workload trace.
solver_feedback.reveals_reference: no — it is an absolute measurement of only the candidate run and contains no reference-relative term.

solver_feedback.name: worst_finish_time_fairness_rho
solver_feedback.means: The candidate's own maximum job-level finish-time-fairness rho for each workload trace.
solver_feedback.reveals_reference: no — rho uses the trace's fixed isolated-runtime and contention normalization, not the reference scheduler's result.

solver_feedback.name: unfair_job_fraction_percent
solver_feedback.means: The candidate's own percentage of jobs above the published rho threshold 1.05 for each workload trace.
solver_feedback.reveals_reference: no — it is computed solely from candidate rhos and the artifact's constant 1.05 threshold, without a reference value.

statement_sentences: In addition to the continuous score, a separate beats-reference criterion compares your scheduler with a withheld reference on the four declared quantities independently on both graded traces. Every one of the eight trace/metric comparisons must strictly improve. The reference values and trace-specific comparison outcomes are not disclosed.
comments: Run candidate and reference with the same original trace, cluster specification, throughput table, Shockwave configuration, time-per-iteration, solver environment, and seed; reject invalid allocations or incomplete runs before metric comparison. Each makespan, average-JCT, worst-rho, and unfair-job-fraction comparison remains strict lower-is-better with no tolerance. Since 2026-09-15, PASS is the conjunction of all eight workload/metric comparisons; a 7/8 result fails. The continuous 40/40/15/5 score uses smooth absolute candidate-only terms, has no artificial upper clipping, preserves raw output, and does not normalize against the reference. Do not expose ratios, differences, margins, reference-normalized scores, workload-specific pass/fail results, or reference values; return only the candidate four absolute per-trace measurements. The unfair-job fraction uses the artifact strict rho > 1.05 test and two-decimal rounding for both candidate and reference.
